name: Worst Idea First

scoring.report_note: Report group-level deltas only. Never rank groups or individuals — the round measures the room's safety, not wit.

description: Two-minute pre/post measure for the Worst Idea First reverse-brainstorm. Scores at group level: how did saying awkward things, risk naming and safety to be specific change across the round?

instructions.pre: Before groups form. Each participant answers alone, about their own last week at work — not about the exercise.
instructions.post: Immediately after the debrief. Same items, now answered about the round just completed, as a group.

items.pre_text: I say the awkward thing in meetings, not after them.
items.post_text: During the worst round, awkward things got said inside the game.

items.pre_text: I name risks before they happen, not in the post-mortem.
items.post_text: The worst ideas named real risks — before any of them happened.

items.pre_text: I keep the risky half of my opinion to myself.
items.post_text: There was a worst idea I thought of and did not say.

items.pre_text: My feedback is specific enough to act on.
items.post_text: The flipped actions were specific: owners, dates, one line each.

items.pre_text: Playfulness helps my team say true things.
items.post_text: The laughter made the room more honest, not less.

items.pre_text: When I spot a failure mode, I can flip it into a preventive action.
items.post_text: Flipping worst to prevent came naturally by the second round.

report.title: Worst Idea First — group safety delta
sections: Worst ideas generated: count, specificity, disguised complaints surfaced
